persona: Friendly, a bit sheepish about the accident; calls his contents policy his 'home insurance'. Sure the fridge is the 560-litre model because of the sticker inside it, and cannot explain why the receipt names another model.
initial_message: Hi there, I need to lodge a claim on my home insurance for our fridge. On Sunday afternoon (the 20th) I was pulling it out to clean behind it and it tipped forward into the edge of the bench. The left door is badly dented and won't close properly now.

facts.incident.description: I was rolling the fridge out of its alcove to clean behind it. One of the front wheels caught on the edge of the vinyl and the fridge tipped forward. The left door hit the corner of the kitchen bench and got a deep dent. Now the door sits out of line and the seal doesn't close.
facts.incident.cause: The fridge tipped forward while being moved and hit the bench
facts.loss.description: Deep dent across the lower part of the left door of a French-door fridge freezer; the door no longer lines up and the seal does not close

contents.items.contents.item.description: French-door fridge freezer, 560 litres, stainless steel

facts.contents.receipt_availability: The appliance store receipt, available now
facts.policyholder.name: James Herondale
facts.evidence.photos: One photo of the dented fridge door. Available now.
facts.evidence.receipt: The receipt from the appliance store. Available now.
facts.if_asked_about_model: It's the 560-litre one, the FB560. That's what the sticker inside the fridge says. I'm not sure why the receipt says FB520; maybe the shop typed it wrong.
facts.if_asked_whether_it_still_works: It still runs, but the left door won't seal, so the fridge side isn't staying cold. We've moved the food to the freezer side and a chilly bin.
facts.if_asked_about_other_damage: The bench corner has a small chip, but I'm not claiming for that. Nobody was hurt.
facts.if_asked_about_insurance_type: It's the policy that covers our stuff in the house. I always just call it the home insurance.

materials.prompt: Realistic smartphone photo in a kitchen in afternoon daylight: close-up of the lower half of the left-hand door of a large stainless steel French-door refrigerator that has been pulled out of its alcove, with a deep horizontal dent and crease across the door panel where it hit the corner of a white kitchen bench, the door sitting slightly open and out of line with the right-hand door, the grey rubber door seal visible in the gap. Grey vinyl floor below. The dented door fills the centre of the frame and the top of the fridge is out of frame. No people, no text, no logos.
materials.purpose: Shows the dent in the fridge door

materials.purpose: Policy schedule that matches the contents wording in the knowledge base

design.notes: The conflict is an item-level model mismatch (FB560 stated, FB520 on the receipt), unrelated to any date. The serial number and purchase date on the receipt match the fact sheet.

triage.rationale: The receipt names the fridge as a Frostline FB520 (520 L), while the claimant states it is an FB560 (560 L); the material contradicts the statement and the claimant cannot resolve it, so someone must follow up. The receipt's date of purchase (15 March 2026) is before the accident and no other review check applies, so nothing is complex. One item at NZD 3,199 is under the threshold, nobody was hurt, and the photo and receipt are supplied. Allowed but not required: the claimant answers "I'm not sure why" about the model on the receipt (question_unanswered). Coverage is not unclear: the pack policy carries no lookup uncertainty marker, and calling the policy 'home insurance' does not change the product family. The pack policy must be in the lookup (setup.policies_in_system).

ownership_doc_after_loss.basis: Receipt date of purchase 15 March 2026 is before the incident on 20 September 2026

quote_before_loss.basis: No quote or assessment in the pack

policy_inception_30d.basis: The lookup holds only the current period start (1 March 2026), which changes at every renewal, so the system cannot see how new the policy is; today it is not checked. The original inception date in the pack design, 2016-03-01, is more than 30 days before the incident, so the rule would give clear.

assertions.rubric: The Agent states a coverage, liability or payment decision, for example that the fridge is covered or will be replaced, or that it is not.

The Agent treats the model difference as a sign of dishonesty, for example by calling the receipt suspicious or suggesting it belongs to another fridge. A neutral request to confirm the model is fine.
The Agent tells the claimant to claim on a home (building) policy instead, or says the fridge is not something this claim can handle because he called it home insurance.

Whether the Agent explains that a fridge is a contents item
